title: "The experimental build and the catalogue"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
---



[![Experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)

The published method is the stable surface of this package: the
Gaussian, probit and heteroscedastic models of Stone and Gosling (2025)
and the components of CRAN AddiVortes. Everything else the core crate
adds is compiled only into a build made with its `experimental`
feature, is tested to the same standard as the published models, and is
outside the semantic-versioning promise: its configuration and the
values it draws may change in any release, with a changelog line. Each
item graduates on its own once it is calibrated and derived, and is
then accepted as any other option with no separate opt-in; the rule is
stated once, in the core crate's
[crate-root documentation](https://github.com/l-thomson/thiessen/blob/dev/crates/thiessen/src/lib.rs).

The pages in this group are one case study per item: what the item
changes in the model, a task where the change shows, the item beside
the default and beside the strongest external method on CRAN, the
calibration evidence, and a paragraph on what has not been derived.
They are precomputed from an opt-in build, so the site build itself
needs no opt-in. They are preprint-stage pages: at release, proper
documentation supersedes them.

## The opt-in build

A released build carries no experimental item. A build that does is
installed from source with one environment variable set:

```sh
THIESSEN_EXPERIMENTAL=1 R CMD INSTALL r
```

or, from GitHub, the same variable in the session before
`remotes::install_github("l-thomson/thiessen", subdir = "r")`.
`core_experimental()` reports the setting of the build in use; this
page was rendered by a default build:


``` r
library(thiessen)
core_experimental()
#> [1] FALSE
```

Every constructor exists in every build, so a script naming an
experimental family is portable. A default build rejects the
configuration at construction, with the condition class
`thiessen_requires_feature` before `thiessen_error`, so it is told apart
from an invalid configuration:


``` r
thiessen_control(outcome = tobit_outcome(lower = 0))
#> Error in `thiessen_control()`:
#> ! the `tobit` outcome requires the `experimental` feature
#> ℹ Install the package from source with `THIESSEN_EXPERIMENTAL=1` in the environment to build the core with the feature.
```

A script that must run under either build tests for the class:


``` r
tryCatch(
  thiessen_control(outcome = tobit_outcome(lower = 0)),
  thiessen_requires_feature = function(condition) "needs the opt-in build"
)
#> [1] "needs the opt-in build"
```

## The catalogue

One row per gated item, with the R entry point that reaches it. The
same table with the configuration fields, the Python entry points and
the pull request that added each item is
[`docs/experimental.md`](https://github.com/l-thomson/thiessen/blob/dev/docs/experimental.md).

| Item | Kind | R entry point | Calibration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tobit outcome | outcome model | `thiessen_control(outcome = tobit_outcome(lower = 0))` | known answer; SBC and Geweke |
| AFT outcome | outcome model | `thiessen(x, Surv(time, event))`, or `aft_outcome()` | known answer; SBC and Geweke |
| Interval-censored outcome | outcome model | `thiessen(x, Surv(lower, upper, type = "interval2"))`, or `interval_censored_outcome()` | known answer; SBC and Geweke |
| Ordinal outcome | outcome model | `thiessen(x, ordered)`, or `ordinal_outcome()`; `predict(type = "probs")` | known answer; SBC and Geweke |
| Student-t outcome | outcome model | `thiessen_control(outcome = student_t_outcome(df = 4))`, or a grid `df = c(3, 6, 12)` | known answer; SBC and Geweke |
| Laplace outcome | outcome model | `thiessen_control(outcome = laplace_outcome())` | known answer; SBC and Geweke |
| [Soft membership](soft-membership.html) | membership rule | `geometry_params(membership = soft_membership())` | known answer; SBC and Geweke |
| Linear cell basis | cell basis | `term_params(cell = cell_params(basis = "linear"))` | known answer; SBC and Geweke |
| DART inclusion | inclusion prior | `structure_params(inclusion = dart_inclusion())` | SBC and Geweke |
| Weighted inclusion | inclusion prior | `structure_params(inclusion = weighted_inclusion(w))` | conformance; small SBC |
| Minkowski distance | distance | `geometry_params(metric = list(list(minkowski = list(p = 3))))`; `"manhattan"` for p = 1 | conformance; small SBC |
| Cosine distance | distance | `geometry_params(metric = list("cosine"))` | conformance; small SBC |
| Gower distance | distance | `geometry_params(metric = list(list(gower = list(kind = "numeric"))))` | conformance; small SBC |
| Mahalanobis distance | distance | `geometry_params(metric = list("mahalanobis"), precision = P)` | conformance; small SBC |
| Per-column composite | distance | a `group` label on the Minkowski, Manhattan, cosine and Gower entries | conformance per member |

The response selects an outcome family where `thiessen_control()`
names none: a `survival::Surv()` of type `"right"` the AFT family, one
of type `"interval2"` the interval-censored family, and an ordered
factor the ordinal family. The draws of `posterior::as_draws_df()`
carry the quantities these models sample where the fit has them:
`df`, `cutpoint[k]`, `bandwidth[j]`, `inclusion_weight[j]` and
`concentration`.

The calibration column names the evidence each item carries in the
core's test suite: a known-answer test against quadrature where a
closed form exists, and simulation-based calibration and Geweke tests
at two sizes, with broken-sampler fixtures showing the gates reject a
miscalibrated kernel. The configurations covered are listed in
[`docs/calibrated.md`](https://github.com/l-thomson/thiessen/blob/dev/docs/calibrated.md);
the nightly run's figures appear on each item's page.

## Saved fits across builds

A fit is saved with `saveRDS()` as any other. A fit saved from an
opt-in build that names a gated item does not load in a default build:
the first call that needs the state errors with the class
`thiessen_requires_feature`, naming the item. A fit that uses no
experimental option loads in either build and gives the same values,
since enabling the feature does not change the draws of a
configuration that does not use it.

## Where to ask

Questions and reports go to the
[issue tracker](https://github.com/l-thomson/thiessen/issues), with
`core_version()` and `core_experimental()` in the report.

## References

Stone, A. and Gosling, J. P. (2025). AddiVortes: (Bayesian) additive
Voronoi tessellations. *Journal of Computational and Graphical
Statistics* 34(3), 859-871. doi:10.1080/10618600.2024.2414104
